chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ayyub al-Madiny, from Suleyman al-Ja'fary, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the killing of the hoopoe, the shrike, the skua gull, and the honey bee.
ai.seo_question: What birds and insects did the Prophet forbid from being killed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrates a prohibition by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) against killing specific birds and insects, namely the hoopoe, shrike, skua gull, and honey bee. It establishes a legal ruling (hukm) regarding the sanctity of these creatures in Islamic tradition. Within Shia jurisprudence, this narration is often cited to support the concept of *daman* (liability for compensation) for killing protected fauna, reflecting the broader Islamic ethic of environmental stewardship and the intrinsic value of creation as signs of God.
